summary.headline: Runwal Enterprises cut net debt-to-equity to 1.5x from 3.1x, while Q2 FY27 pre-sales rose 26% YoY to Rs 609 crore.
summary.overview: Pre-sales rose to Rs 609 crore in Q2 from Rs 484 crore in Q1, up about 26% sequentially-reported growth figure as stated, with gross collections up 23.5% YoY to Rs 550 crore. Average selling price rose about 12% to Rs 14,907 per sq ft, helped by mix from the 7M Lakshmi project and strata-sold retail and commercial units. Net debt-to-equity fell from 3.1x to 1.5x, driven by conversion of convertible debentures, Rs 500 crore of IPO proceeds recognised in equity, and debt repayment. Deliveries in H1 FY27 were about 1.9 million sq ft versus 0.86 million sq ft in H1 FY26. Management reiterated a full-year pre-sales growth of about 20%, with H2 expected to be stronger.

segments.name: Residential development
segments.commentary: Core business; portfolio of about 75 million sq ft residential, with target mix of roughly one-third each across affordable, mid-income and luxury once launches stabilise. Q2 deliveries helped by Runwal Garden phase 3 occupation certificates.

segments.name: Annuity / commercial and retail
segments.commentary: About 300,000 sq ft of ongoing commercial projects and about 800,000 sq ft of retail mall space, across Runwal BKC and the Dombivli mall. BKC commercial project has no debt; the mall has construction finance of about Rs 106 crore plus NCDs of about Rs 115 crore, totalling about Rs 221 crore of net debt linked to annuity assets.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 pre-sales guidance reiterated at around 20% growth, with a range of roughly Rs 2,500-3,000 crore cited by management.

FY27 revenue recognition expected to be about 10% higher than FY26, with margins reverting to FY26 levels, driven by an income-segment tower in Mumbai expected to receive occupation certificate in H2.
Ready-to-move-in inventory of about 0.38 million sq ft (around 70% in Runwal Mall City cluster 5) expected to be sold by end FY27.
Management indicated growth of roughly 20-25% per year is the target, with FY28 guidance to add about 20% on FY27 base.
Ongoing land parcel monetisation in Mumbai (JLL appointed, around 11-12 interested parties) expected to reduce debt by a decent amount; outcome to be announced soon.
Annual cash flows cited as above Rs 2,000 crore last year, with 20-30% growth expected this year.
capex_capacity: Development area of about 88.37 million sq ft as of September: about 18.1 million sq ft ongoing and about 56 million sq ft upcoming.
Kanjurmarg Runwal Bliss phase 3 already launched; two towers under construction; possible tower 3 launch expected in Q4 FY27.
Chembur (Runwal Woods) project already launched; no further launches planned there.
No planned projects awaiting regulatory approval; no timeline extensions expected on running projects.
Growth strategy favours asset-light JV, JD, redevelopment and partnership models; Dombivli portfolio monetisation under consideration.
demand_pricing: Q3 CY2026 MMR recorded about 31,750 housing units sold (Anarock, as cited), leading the top 7 markets.
Mumbai recorded 3,683 property registrations in the 10-day Diwali period; stamp duty collections up 13% to Rs 384 crore (Knight Frank, as cited).

ASP increase attributed to higher contribution from 7M Lakshmi project and strata sales of retail and commercial units; management expects ASP to stay broadly in the current range on a normalised basis.
Management acknowledged a Quota report showing unsold inventory overhangs across seven cities including Mumbai (about 1.98 lakh units), but argued the ready-to-move-in share is much smaller.

Expansion focus: eastern suburbs (Kalyan, Dombivli, Kanjurmarg, Mulund), with moves into south Mumbai, central Mumbai and western suburbs; Pune and other peripheral cities mentioned as possible but not current focus.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 pre-sales and full-year growth be on track, and will FY27 be a strong year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 20% full-year pre-sales growth, implying roughly Rs 2,500-3,000 crore, with H2 expected to be stronger than H1, as in most developers.

qa_highlights.question: Will net debt fall further over the next 6-9 months given land monetisation options?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; a small acreage parcel in Mumbai is being monetised via JLL with 11-12 interested parties under evaluation, expected to cut debt by a decent amount. Other measures are being evaluated with no significant progress yet.

qa_highlights.question: How is debt split between residential and annuity assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Annuity assets carry about Rs 221 crore of net debt: Rs 106 crore construction finance and about Rs 115 crore NCDs on the mall. BKC commercial project is debt-free; the residential projects hold the rest.

qa_highlights.question: How much completed inventory is unsold and when will it clear?
qa_highlights.answer: About 0.38 million sq ft of ready-to-move-in saleable inventory, about 70% in Runwal Mall City cluster 5 (OC received), expected to be sold by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the launch timelines for Kanjurmarg, Chembur and Mulund projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Chembur project (Runwal Woods) launched with no further launches planned; Kanjurmarg Runwal Bliss phase 3 launched with possible tower 3 launch in Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Are any launches waiting on regulatory approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: No; no planned launches or running projects are awaiting approvals, so no delays expected.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ASP increase and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher contribution from 7M Lakshmi (higher ASP than Mumbai and Dombivli projects) and strata sales of retail/commercial units; ASP expected to stay in a similar range on normalised basis.

risks_watch: Revenue recognition is tied to occupation certificates and handovers, so quarterly reported numbers can swing sharply; H2 revenue depends on an income-segment Mumbai tower receiving OC.
Affordable-segment projects (Runwal Garden, Runwal My City) carry lower gross margins; margin recovery to FY26 levels depends on mix shift.
Net debt reduction beyond the current 1.5x depends on the Mumbai land monetisation outcome and JV/JD deals; no concrete timeline for further steps.
Market oversupply: a Quota report flagged large unsold inventory across seven cities, including Mumbai; management disputed the risk based on ready-inventory share.
Pre-sales guidance of about 20% growth requires a much stronger H2 than H1 (Rs 484 crore Q1 and Rs 609 crore Q2 so far).
summary.management_tone: Confident on balance sheet progress and Mumbai demand, but cautious and vague on revenue timing and specific figures for FY27 guidance, which were given as ranges. Several answers on debt reduction and land monetisation were non-committal, with no firm timeline.
key_quotes: It's my pleasure to inform that we have reduced our net debt from 3.1x to 1.5 at the end of this quarter as indicated by us on the previous call.
A stronger balance sheet gives us greater flexibility to invest into our new projects as well as pursue new opportunities and continue growing without compromising on financial discipline.
We remain focused on capital efficient growth as we had discussed in our previous call.

adds.what: Kanjurmarg Runwal Bliss phase 3 tower 3 launch (launch, not physical capacity)
Income-segment tower in Mumbai expected to receive occupation certificate

growth.why: Management reiterated ~20% FY27 pre-sales growth (Rs 2,500-3,000 crore) and about 10% higher FY27 revenue recognition, backed by Rs 609 crore Q2 pre-sales, 0.38 million sq ft RTMI inventory and an income-segment Mumbai tower due for OC in H2, though no specific sales-to-target bridge was quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects margins to revert to FY26 levels as revenue recognition rises about 10% and the mix shifts away from lower-margin affordable projects (Runwal Garden, My City), though no margin figure was quantified.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Development area is about 88.37 million sq ft (18.1 million ongoing, 56 million upcoming), with Kanjurmarg tower 3 possible in Q4 FY27 and an income-segment Mumbai tower due for OC in H2 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterated about 20% FY27 pre-sales growth (Rs 2,500-3,000 crore) and about 10% higher revenue recognition, but H1 pre-sales are only Rs 1,093 crore (Rs 484 crore plus Rs 609 crore), so H2 must be much stronger.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Growth is being pursued through asset-light JV, JD, redevelopment and partnership models, and Chembur has no further launches, so no new capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only reiterated at about 20% pre-sales growth, with no sign of ahead-of-guidance running; the H2 requirement is demanding.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 pre-sales of Rs 1,093 crore need H2 of about Rs 1,400-1,900 crore to reach Rs 2,500-3,000 crore, and revenue timing depends on OC receipts, with a Quota report flagging Mumbai oversupply.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Kanjurmarg Runwal Bliss tower 3 launch is possible in Q4 FY27, but no new brand or product line was named.

rows.label: Mumbai land parcel monetisation via JLL
rows.why: JLL appointed with 11-12 interested parties, and management said it should cut debt by a decent amount, though no value or timeline was given; net debt-to-equity is already down to 1.5x from 3.1x.

rows.label: Ready-to-move-in inventory sell-down
rows.why: About 0.38 million sq ft of RTMI inventory, around 70% in Runwal Mall City cluster 5 with OC received, is expected to be sold by end FY27.

rows.label: ASP holds at elevated level
rows.why: ASP rose about 12% to Rs 14,907 per sq ft on 7M Lakshmi and strata sales, but management expects it to stay only broadly in the current range on a normalised basis.

tone.note: Management was confident on balance-sheet repair (net debt-to-equity 1.5x from 3.1x) and Mumbai demand, but gave FY27 guidance only as ranges and was non-committal on land monetisation timing; analysts pushed on the H2 ramp needed for the 20% pre-sales target.
